claim: Excessive plasma histamine concentrations cause symptoms in mast cell activation syndrome, mastocytosis, or anaphylaxis.
source: Excessive plasma histamine concentrations cause symptoms in mast cell activation syndrome, mastocytosis, or anaphylaxis.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that draws on established medical knowledge about histamine-related conditions.

claim: Anti-histamines are often insufficiently efficacious for treating conditions with excessive plasma histamine.
source: Anti-histamines are often insufficiently efficacious.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Human diamine oxidase (hDAO) can rapidly degrade histamine.
source: Human diamine oxidase (hDAO) can rapidly degrade histamine and therefore represents a promising new treatment strategy for conditions with pathological histamine concentrations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the manuscript.

claim: Recombinant hDAO is rapidly cleared from the circulation in rats and mice.
source: Recombinant hDAO is rapidly cleared from the circulation in rats and mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vivo studies presented in the manuscript.

claim: After mutation of the heparin-binding motif, binding to heparin and heparan sulfate was strongly reduced.
source: After mutation of the heparin-binding motif, binding to heparin and heparan sulfate was strongly reduced.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from binding assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: The double mutant rhDAO-R568S/R571T showed minimal cellular uptake.
source: The double mutant rhDAO-R568S/R571T showed minimal cellular uptake.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cellular uptake assays.

claim: The short α-distribution half-life of the wildtype protein was eliminated by mutation of the heparin-binding motif.
source: The short α-distribution half-life of the wildtype protein was eliminated, and the clearance was significantly reduced in rodents.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic data from rodent studies.

claim: The clearance of rhDAO was significantly reduced in rodents after mutation of the heparin-binding motif.
source: The short α-distribution half-life of the wildtype protein was eliminated, and the clearance was significantly reduced in rodents.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic data from rodent studies.

claim: Histamine acts mainly on vascular endothelial, bronchial, and smooth muscle cells after activation of histamine receptors 1 and 2.
source: Following activation of the histamine receptors 1 and 2, histamine acts mainly on vascular endothelial, bronchial, and smooth muscle cells and causes symptoms affecting the cardiovascular system, the skin, and the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts (Jutel et al., 2009; Valent et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Histamine induces nitric oxide synthesis, which causes vasodilation, vascular hyperpermeability, edema formation, and hypotension.
source: It induces nitric oxide synthesis, which causes vasodilation, vascular hyperpermeability, edema formation, and consequently hypotension (Ashina et al., 2015; Claesson-Welsh, 2015; Pober and Sessa, 2015; Valent et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The development of hypotension strongly correlates with histamine concentrations.
source: The development of hypotension strongly correlates with histamine concentrations (Kaliner et al., 1982).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In severe anaphylaxis, mean histamine concentrations of 140 ng/mL have been measured.
source: In severe anaphylaxis, mean histamine concentrations of 140 ng/mL have been measured (van der Linden et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Human diamine oxidase is a homodimer encoded by the AOC1 gene.
source: The copper-containing amine oxidase human diamine oxidase (hDAO; E.C. 1.4.3.6) is a homodimer encoded by the AOC1 gene (Barbry et al., 1990; Chassande et al., 1994)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: hDAO is highly expressed in the intestine, kidneys, and extravillous trophoblasts.
source: which is highly expressed in the intestine (Wollin et al., 1998), the kidneys (Schwelberger et al., 1998), and extravillous trophoblasts (Velicky et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In pregnancy serum, hDAO at a mean concentration of 125 ng/mL rapidly degraded 100 ng/mL histamine with a half-life of 3.4 min.
source: In pregnancy serum, hDAO at a mean concentration of 125 ng/mL rapidly degraded 100 ng/mL histamine with a half-life of 3.4 min (Boehm et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In the 1930s, porcine diamine oxidase was used to treat histamine-related pathologies with limited success.
source: In the 1930s, porcine diamine oxidase was already used to treat histamine-related pathologies with limited success (Laymon and Cumming, 1939; Miller and Piness, 1940).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: After intravenous infusion of recombinant hDAO in rats and mice, the half-life was less than 5 min.
source: After intravenous infusion of recombinant hDAO (rhDAO) in rats and mice, the half-life was less than 5 min (Gludovacz et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The rapid clearance of rhDAO was not caused by binding of the N-glycans to the asialoglycoprotein- or the mannose-receptor.
source: The rapid clearance was not caused by binding of the N-glycans to the asialoglycoprotein- or the mannose-receptor.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior experimental work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Diamine oxidase was internalized by various epithelial and endothelial cell lines.
source: Diamine oxidase did not only bind to but was also internalized by various epithelial and endothelial cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior experimental work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Internalization of diamine oxidase was inhibited by high molecular weight heparin.
source: Internalization was inhibited by high molecular weight heparin (HMWH), and glycosaminoglycan- and heparan sulfate (HS)-deficient CHO cell lines were incapable of rhDAO uptake.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior experimental work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Glycosaminoglycan- and heparan sulfate-deficient CHO cell lines were incapable of rhDAO uptake.
source: Internalization was inhibited by high molecular weight heparin (HMWH), and glycosaminoglycan- and heparan sulfate (HS)-deficient CHO cell lines were incapable of rhDAO uptake.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior experimental work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Diamine oxidase is produced by intestinal and proximal tubular kidney epithelial cells.
source: Diamine oxidase is produced by intestinal and proximal tubular kidney epithelial cells and binds to the basolateral membranes in the lamina propria after secretion into the interstitial compartment and in vitro also to endothelial cells (Schwelberger et al., 1999; Wollin et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Diamine oxidase binds to the basolateral membranes in the lamina propria after secretion into the interstitial compartment.
source: Diamine oxidase is produced by intestinal and proximal tubular kidney epithelial cells and binds to the basolateral membranes in the lamina propria after secretion into the interstitial compartment and in vitro also to endothelial cells (Schwelberger et al., 1999; Wollin et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Diamine oxidase binds to endothelial cells in vitro.
source: Diamine oxidase is produced by intestinal and proximal tubular kidney epithelial cells and binds to the basolateral membranes in the lamina propria after secretion into the interstitial compartment and in vitro also to endothelial cells (Schwelberger et al., 1999; Wollin et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Diamine oxidase is released from its binding sites by heparin infusion, resulting in an increase in plasma activity.
source: It is released from its binding sites by heparin infusion, resulting in an increase in plasma activity (Biebl et al., 2002; D'Agostino et al., 1989; Gäng et al., 1975; Hansson and Thysell, 1973; Klocker et al., 2004; Klocker et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Robinson-White et al. described the binding of rat placental DAO to rat and guinea pig microvascular endothelial cells and its displacement by heparin.
source: Robinson-White et al. described the binding of rat placental DAO to rat and guinea pig microvascular endothelial cells and its displacement by heparin, indicating that DAO binds to cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPG) (Robinson-White et al., 1985).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: DAO binds to cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans.
source: Robinson-White et al. described the binding of rat placental DAO to rat and guinea pig microvascular endothelial cells and its displacement by heparin, indicating that DAO binds to cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPG) (Robinson-White et al., 1985).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature and inference from the displacement by heparin.

claim: During anaphylaxis, secretion of heparin from mast cells likely results in DAO release from HSPG located in the extracellular matrix or on the surface of gastrointestinal epithelial cells.
source: During anaphylaxis, secretion of heparin from MCs likely results in DAO release from HSPG located in the extracellular matrix or on the surface of gastrointestinal epithelial cells (Boehm et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim involves speculation about the mechanism during anaphylaxis, supported by a citation.

claim: Cell surface HSPG probably mediate cellular binding and/or uptake of rhDAO.
source: Cell surface HSPG probably mediate cellular binding and/or uptake of rhDAO.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on prior observations.

claim: Novotny et al., 1994 proposed that the amino acids 568–575 or RFKRKLPK constitute a heparin-binding motif.
source: Novotny et al., 1994 proposed that the amino acids 568–575 or RFKRKLPK constitute a heparin-binding motif (HBM) (Novotny et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The amino acid stretches 568-575 form a ring-like structure including the motifs of both monomers on the surface of DAO.
source: These amino acid stretches form a ring-like structure including the motifs of both monomers on the surface of DAO (McGrath et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: No negatively charged amino acids are close to the positively charged ring structure of the heparin-binding motif.
source: No negatively charged amino acids are close to this positively charged ring structure (McGrath et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The putative heparin-binding site of hDAO possesses the size, shape, and electrostatic properties suitable for heparin and HS binding.
source: The putative heparin-binding site of hDAO possesses the size, shape, and electrostatic properties suitable for heparin and HS binding (Gludovacz et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: It has never been demonstrated, neither in vitro nor in vivo, that the RFKRKLPK sequence mediates heparin and HS binding.
source: However, it has never been demonstrated, neither in vitro nor in vivo, that the RFKRKLPK sequence mediates heparin and HS binding.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of prior evidence.

claim: The short half-life of rhDAO in rats and mice is highly unfavorable for the development of rhDAO as a new treatment option for diseases with rapid and excessive histamine release.
source: The short half-life of rhDAO in rats and mice is highly unfavorable for the development of rhDAO as a new treatment option for diseases with rapid and excessive histamine release from MCs or basophils.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pharmacokinetic data and the therapeutic goal.

claim: rhDAO rapidly degrades pathophysiologically relevant histamine concentrations.
source: We herein demonstrate for the first time that rhDAO rapidly degrades pathophysiologically relevant histamine concentrations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The RFKRKLPK sequence mediates heparin binding.
source: Using appropriate mutations in the RFKRKLPK sequence, we prove the heparin binding function of this ring structure motif and its involvement in the ultra-rapid plasma clearance of rhDAO.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mutation studies.

claim: The RFKRKLPK sequence is involved in the ultra-rapid plasma clearance of rhDAO.
source: Using appropriate mutations in the RFKRKLPK sequence, we prove the heparin binding function of this ring structure motif and its involvement in the ultra-rapid plasma clearance of rhDAO.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mutation studies.

claim: The HBM mutants show a strongly decreased binding to heparin and HS.
source: The HBM mutants show a strongly decreased binding to heparin and HS, minimal cellular internalization, and a strong reduction of the in vivo clearance in rodents with unchanged catalytic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from binding assays.

claim: The HBM mutants show minimal cellular internalization.
source: The HBM mutants show a strongly decreased binding to heparin and HS, minimal cellular internalization, and a strong reduction of the in vivo clearance in rodents with unchanged catalytic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cellular uptake assays.

claim: The HBM mutants show a strong reduction of the in vivo clearance in rodents.
source: The HBM mutants show a strongly decreased binding to heparin and HS, minimal cellular internalization, and a strong reduction of the in vivo clearance in rodents with unchanged catalytic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pharmacokinetic studies in rodents.

claim: The HBM mutants have unchanged catalytic activity compared to wildtype rhDAO.
source: The HBM mutants show a strongly decreased binding to heparin and HS, minimal cellular internalization, and a strong reduction of the in vivo clearance in rodents with unchanged catalytic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing enzymatic activity.

claim: 6 nM rhDAO-WT completely degraded 100 ng/mL histamine in less than 15 min using 1% HSA-PBS or EDTA plasma.
source: 6 nM (1 µg/mL) rhDAO-WT with and without a 100-fold molar excess of HMWH completely degraded 100 ng/mL histamine in less than 15 min using 1% HSA-PBS or EDTA plasma (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Heparin did not influence DAO activity.
source: Heparin did not influence DAO activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing DAO activity with and without heparin.

claim: rhDAO-WT degraded exogenous and endogenous histamine to harmless concentrations below 1 ng/mL in plasma of mastocytosis patients and healthy volunteers.
source: rhDAO-WT degraded exogenous and endogenous histamine to harmless concentrations below 1 ng/mL.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from plasma samples.

claim: Histamine deamination was completely blocked by addition of the potent DAO inhibitor DIMAZ.
source: Histamine deamination was completely blocked by addition of the potent DAO inhibitor DIMAZ (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The tested HBM mutants eluted from the heparin-sepharose at lower salt concentrations than the wildtype protein.
source: The tested HBM mutants eluted from the heparin-sepharose at lower salt concentrations than the wildtype protein (Figure 2 and Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and Table 1.

claim: rhDAO-R568S/R571T demonstrated the weakest binding to heparin-sepharose.
source: rhDAO-R568S/R571T demonstrated the weakest binding to heparin-sepharose and was therefore further analyzed using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and biolayer interferometry (BLI).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from heparin-sepharose binding assays.

claim: rhDAO-WT bound to HMWH with mean KD values of 634 nM in ITC and 1.6 and 69 nM in BLI analyses.
source: rhDAO-WT bound to HMWH with mean (SD) KD values of 634 (26) nM in ITC and 1.6 and 69 nM in BLI analyses with likely two DAO molecules binding to one HMWH molecule (Gludovacz et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Two DAO molecules likely bind to one HMWH molecule.
source: rhDAO-WT bound to HMWH with mean (SD) KD values of 634 (26) nM in ITC and 1.6 and 69 nM in BLI analyses with likely two DAO molecules binding to one HMWH molecule (Gludovacz et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature and involves inference from binding data.

claim: The mean KD values for HS binding by rhDAO-WT were 4 and 112 nM using BLI.
source: The mean KD values for HS were 4 and 112 nM using BLI.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The best curve fit for HS binding was generated with a ratio of two molecules DAO binding to one molecule HS.
source: The best curve fit was again generated with a ratio of two molecules DAO binding to one molecule HS (Gludovacz et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature and involves inference from binding data.

claim: rhDAO-R568S/R571T did not show any binding to HMWH.
source: rhDAO-R568S/R571T, the rhDAO mutant with the lowest heparin affinity, did not show any binding to HMWH and only minimal binding to HS (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: rhDAO-R568S/R571T showed only minimal binding to HS.
source: rhDAO-R568S/R571T, the rhDAO mutant with the lowest heparin affinity, did not show any binding to HMWH and only minimal binding to HS (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: SK-Hep1 cells showed a slightly reduced uptake of the single mutant rhDAO-R568S.
source: SK-Hep1 cells showed a slightly reduced uptake of the single mutant rhDAO-R568S, but a strong decrease for both double mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SK-Hep1 cells showed a strong decrease in uptake for both double mutants rhDAO-R568S/R571T and rhDAO-R568S/K575T.
source: SK-Hep1 cells showed a slightly reduced uptake of the single mutant rhDAO-R568S, but a strong decrease for both double mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The wildtype protein showed intracellular granular staining in fluorescence microscopy.
source: The wildtype protein showed intracellular granular staining.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The fluorescence signal using the rhDAO-R568S/R571T mutant was comparable to the negative controls with no DAO added.
source: The fluorescence signal using the mutant was comparable to the negative controls with no DAO added (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In flow cytometric analyses, the reduction in fluorescence of the double mutant rhDAO-R568S/R571T ranged from 67% in SK-Hep1 to 85% in PODO/TERT256 cells.
source: In flow cytometric analyses, the reduction in fluorescence of the double mutant rhDAO-R568S/R571T ranged from 67% in SK-Hep1 to 85% in PODO/TERT256 cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The decrease in fluorescence intensity was statistically significant for all cell lines (p-value<0.05).
source: The decrease in fluorescence intensity was statistically significant for all cell lines (p-value<0.05; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The mean uptake of the single mutant rhDAO-R568S was reduced by 29–71% in western blot analyses.
source: The mean (SEM) uptake of the single mutant was reduced by only 29–71% (9%), while the band intensities of rhDAO-R568S/R571T and rhDAO-R568S/K575T decreased more than fivefold to 17% (5%) and 18% (3%), respectively (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The band intensities of rhDAO-R568S/R571T and rhDAO-R568S/K575T decreased more than fivefold to 17% and 18%, respectively, in western blot analyses.
source: The mean (SEM) uptake of the single mutant was reduced by only 29–71% (9%), while the band intensities of rhDAO-R568S/R571T and rhDAO-R568S/K575T decreased more than fivefold to 17% (5%) and 18% (3%), respectively (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The double mutant rhDAO-R568S/R571T generated the highest area under the curve in rats.
source: The double mutant rhDAO-R568S/R571T generated the highest area under the curve (AUC), followed by rhDAO-R568S and rhDAO-R568S/K575T (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacokinetic data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: An rhFc-DAO wildtype fusion protein and the corresponding rhFc-DAO-R568S/R571T mutant confirmed the improved pharmacokinetic parameters.
source: We also tested an rhFc-DAO wildtype fusion protein and the corresponding rhFc-DAO-R568S/R571T mutant confirming the improved pharmacokinetic parameters (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacokinetic data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: rhDAO-R568S/R571T mutant increases the area under the curve more than 15-fold compared to wildtype rhDAO after intravenous injection into mice.
source: The most promising variant rhDAO-R568S/R571T was also tested in mice, and the data support the rat data with more than 15-fold increases in the AUC after intravenous or intraperitoneal administration (Figure 4C and D and Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacokinetic data shown in Figure 4C and D and Table 2.

claim: rhDAO-R568S/R571T mutant increases the area under the curve more than 15-fold compared to wildtype rhDAO after intraperitoneal injection into mice.
source: The most promising variant rhDAO-R568S/R571T was also tested in mice, and the data support the rat data with more than 15-fold increases in the AUC after intravenous or intraperitoneal administration (Figure 4C and D and Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacokinetic data shown in Figure 4C and D and Table 2.

claim: The rhDAO-R568S/R571T mutant degraded histamine as efficiently as wildtype DAO using 6 nM enzyme concentration.
source: The rhDAO-R568S/R571T mutant with and without a 100-fold molar excess of HMWH degraded histamine as efficiently as wildtype DAO using 1 µg/mL or 6 nM enzyme concentration (Figure 5A compared to WT in Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A compared to Figure 1A.

claim: No significant differences in enzymatic activity could be detected comparing rhDAO-WT and -R568S/R571T mutant at concentrations of 0.7, 2, and 6 nM.
source: No significant differences in enzymatic activity could be detected comparing rhDAO-WT and -R568S/R571T mutant at concentrations of 0.7, 2, and 6 nM using a different assay format (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: After intravenous administration of rhDAO-R568S/R571T, rhDAO-R568S/K575T, and the Fc fusion protein Fc-R568S/R571T, the corresponding DAO activity could be readily measured for 28 hr.
source: After intravenous administration of rhDAO-R568S/R571T, rhDAO-R568S/K575T, and the Fc fusion protein Fc-R568S/R571T, the corresponding DAO activity could be readily measured for 28 hr (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Diamine oxidase concentrations and activities are highly correlated with R2 values of >96%.
source: Diamine oxidase concentrations and activities are highly correlated with R2 values of >96% (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The symmetric HBM on top of the DAO dimer is composed of the residues 568RFKRKLPK575 from both chains.
source: The symmetric HBM on top of the DAO dimer is composed of the residues 568RFKRKLPK575 from both chains (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 10 out of 16 residues (63%) in the HBM are positively charged.
source: with 10 out of 16 residues (63%) positively charged.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the structural composition of the HBM.

claim: The experimental results demonstrated that R568 is critical for heparin binding.
source: The experimental results demonstrated that R568 is critical for heparin binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mutation studies.

claim: The replacement of R568 by a serine was predicted to strongly decrease the binding affinity.
source: The replacement of R568 by a serine (Figure 6B) was predicted to strongly decrease the binding affinity, while the variants R571T (Figure 6C) and K575T (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C) were predicted to be associated with lower binding energy changes (Table 3), supporting the experimental binding data using heparin-sepharose (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by in silico predictions shown in Table 3.

claim: The variants R571T and K575T were predicted to be associated with lower binding energy changes.
source: The replacement of R568 by a serine (Figure 6B) was predicted to strongly decrease the binding affinity, while the variants R571T (Figure 6C) and K575T (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C) were predicted to be associated with lower binding energy changes (Table 3), supporting the experimental binding data using heparin-sepharose (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by in silico predictions shown in Table 3.

claim: The squared correlation coefficient from regression analysis using affinity predictions and measured salt elution concentrations was 93% (p-value 0.0088) including wildtype and four HBM mutants but excluding the triple mutant.
source: The squared correlation coefficient from regression analysis using affinity predictions and measured salt elution concentrations was 93% (p-value 0.0088) including wildtype and four HBM mutants but excluding the triple mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: R568s form hydrogen bonds with heparin hexasaccharide.
source: In both rhDAO chains, R568 forms ionic interactions and hydrogen bonds with the sulfate groups of the heparin hexasaccharide (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by in silico modeling shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: These interactions are absent in the R568S mutant.
source: These interactions are absent in the R568S mutant (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by in silico modeling shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The R571 residue has a role in the overall architecture of the HBM since its guanidinium group forms intra-chain hydrogen bonds.
source: The R571 residue has a role in the overall architecture of the HBM since its guanidinium group forms intra-chain hydrogen bonds (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), which are lost in the R571T mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by in silico modeling shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and 1E.

claim: The intra-chain hydrogen bonds formed by R571 are lost in the R571T mutant.
source: The R571 residue has a role in the overall architecture of the HBM since its guanidinium group forms intra-chain hydrogen bonds (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), which are lost in the R571T mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by in silico modeling shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and 1E.

claim: The negligible effect of K575T change on binding affinity can be attributed to its deep location and long distance from the heparin hexasaccharide.
source: The negligible effect of K575T change on binding affinity can be attributed to its deep location and long distance from the heparin hexasaccharide.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis.

claim: The destabilizing effect of K575T likely results from the loss of favorable intramolecular interactions formed by K575.
source: The destabilizing effect (Table 3) likely results from the loss of favorable intramolecular interactions formed by K575 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis shown in Table 3 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The triple mutant K570G/R571Q/K572T showed the lowest predicted affinity of all mutants.
source: Although the triple mutant K570G/R571Q/K572T (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G) showed the lowest predicted affinity of all mutants, binding to heparin-sepharose was stronger compared to R568S/R571T (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by in silico predictions shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: Binding to heparin-sepharose was stronger for the triple mutant K570G/R571Q/K572T compared to R568S/R571T.
source: Although the triple mutant K570G/R571Q/K572T (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G) showed the lowest predicted affinity of all mutants, binding to heparin-sepharose was stronger compared to R568S/R571T (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: The discrepancy between predicted and experimental binding for the triple mutant might be explained by the additive nature of the energy change calculating algorithm, which is functionally optimized for single and double point mutations and likely overestimates the effects of triple mutations.
source: This discrepancy might be explained by the additive nature of the energy change calculating algorithm, which is functionally optimized for single and double point mutations and likely overestimates the effects of triple mutations (Spassov and Yan, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of the computational method, supported by a citation.

claim: Due to the surface position of R568, K570, R571, and K572, the effects of their mutations on the structural stability, even in the case of the triple mutant, are predicted to be lower.
source: Due to the surface position of R568, K570, R571, and K572, the effects of their mutations on the structural stability, even in the case of the triple mutant, are predicted to be lower (Table 3, Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis shown in Table 3 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: Plasma histamine concentrations of at least 500 ng/mL were measured in a systemic mastocytosis patient following gastrointestinal endoscopy.
source: Plasma histamine concentrations of at least 500 ng/mL (4.5 µM) were measured in a systemic mastocytosis patient following gastrointestinal endoscopy (Desborough et al., 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Circulatory collapse occurred in a mastocytosis patient with 70 ng/mL plasma histamine.
source: We recently published data on the circulatory collapse in a mastocytosis patients with 70 ng/mL plasma histamine (Boehm et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Histamine concentrations in a systemic mastocytosis patient increased from 10 ng/mL to 35 ng/mL over a few hours, and the patient developed severe clinical symptoms despite high-dose treatment with histamine receptor antagonists.
source: Histamine concentrations in another systemic mastocytosis patient increased from 10 ng/mL to 35 ng/mL over a few hours. The patient developed severe clinical symptoms despite high-dose treatment with the histamine receptor 1 antagonist diphenhydramine and the histamine receptor 2 antagonist ranitidine (Boehm et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Approximately 70% of mastocytosis patients define themselves as disabled despite treatment with histamine receptor antagonists up to four times the approved dose and the use of additional medications.
source: Despite treatment with histamine receptor antagonists up to four times the approved dose and the use of additional medications, approximately 70% of mastocytosis patients define themselves as disabled in accordance with standard definitions of disability (Hermine et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: 25–33% of chronic urticaria patients are resistant to histamine receptor antagonists.
source: Finally, 25–33% of chronic urticaria patients are resistant to histamine receptor antagonists (van den Elzen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In healthy volunteers, two combinations of histamine receptor antagonists were only able to sufficiently block symptom development until systemic histamine concentrations of approximately 6 ng/mL were reached.
